localBiteReport: The Choctawhatchee Bay and Destin inshore fishery is in one of its better stretches of the year heading into late September, with the early-fall transition well underway. Capt. Adam Schroeder of Ignite The Bite Charters (Destin) reported last week that bait has become plentiful and easy to locate each morning, and described the current inshore bite as among the best he has seen all year — with redfish, flounder, and speckled trout all responding. Both slot-sized and bull redfish are active around the Destin and Fort Walton area bridges on outgoing tides, with croakers and spot minnows the preferred live-bait choice for targeting larger reds; flounder are mixed in as a reliable bonus species when targeting similar structure. Water temp at the bay is 86°F. The September 4–10 report (one week prior) similarly noted that concentrations of greenies and other bait were pushing from deeper open water onto flats, bayous, and bridge areas in Choctawhatchee Bay, which was already improving the Spanish mackerel bite and setting up better conditions for trout and reds on the flats — a pattern that the following week's report confirms has continued to mature.
